_comment: Fighting withdrawal under a plain MOVE order: two even Infantry regiments spawn 200wu apart (staging borrowed from disengage-step-back.json -- the enemy AI closes and locks both in melee under its own order, contact lands ~tick 183). At tick 300, with the block fully engaged, the player right-clicks EMPTY GROUND well behind the line: a plain MOVE into the rear sector. Before this fix the engaged unit obeyed by centre-pivot-turning inside the press -- its slot grid swung across the whole block depth while phantom ramp-up speed throttled the pivot, so the melee-scattered bodies stacked (nnd_min ~0.1-0.7wu against a 2.25 threshold) chasing slots they could never settle onto. Now the disciplined block peels straight BACK holding the facing it fought in -- taking rear strikes for it, the documented cost of disengaging against an unbroken pursuer -- while every soldier tracks the slot grid it would have if still standing. The clip ends mid-withdrawal, before morale breaks; the drilled about-face that completes the move once contact clears is covered by the unit suite. State dumps verify: post-click facing stays (0,1) while the regiment backs north, and nearest-neighbour spacing never collapses.
